analysis:
This batch contains only documentation: a new changelog fragment (changelog.d/coordinator-traffic-verdict.md, lines 1-5) and an addition to docs/provider/cli-reference.md (a Traffic: status line description near head lines 998-1009, plus a date bump). No executable source is supplied, so the described behavior (the Traffic status line and doctor check, the coordinator_connection field in the daemon state file, and idle-gated re-registration at 15-30 min, 30 min, 1 h, 2 h, then every 4 h) is unverified against code.

Security-relevant points for later review of the code PR:
(1) Re-registration starts a new coordinator verification session. This relates to TB-002, TB-011, T-053 and T-057. Reviewers should confirm that it re-proves custody of the process key, does not extend or reuse an old App Attest lease or grant, and gets a fresh socket nonce. It must not bypass the T-053 binding and revocation checks, and it must not become a way to force repeated re-verification or retry storms. It should wait for idle (no accepted or local requests, loads, drain, update) so it does not drop in-flight inference and cause a DoS (T-010, T-057).
(2) The Traffic diagnostics echo the coordinator's reasons (locked keychain, stalled Apple call, no linked account) in status and doctor output. Confirm that no tokens, stable key, account or machine identifiers, or receipts are printed, in line with T-058. Confirm that coordinator-supplied reason strings are sanitized or bounded before being written to the terminal or logs.
(3) The coordinator_connection field in the state file should carry only timestamps and counters, and the file should keep owner-only permissions.
(4) The Traffic line is advisory display. It must not be treated as serving authorization (T-052), and the eligible wording must not overclaim runtime secrecy (T-056).

No concrete regression is evident from the documentation alone.
